1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night

The rain over Ishikawa had been falling for three days now. Haruka Sato's older sister had left for the capital in the spring, and since then, Haruka had been running the small pharmacy in town all by herself.
When night fell, he closed the storm shutters, counted the day's receipts, blew out the lamp, and went up to the second floor.
The moment she lay down, there was the sound of someone pounding violently on a door below, and a man's voice called out. "Is anyone there?"

A young man, soaked to the bone, stood in the doorway. Blood seeped through the cloth wrapped around his left arm. The man gave his name as Ken'ichi Mori and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"I'd like to have my wound treated," Mori said in a low voice. "I'll pay the fee. Will 3,500 yen be enough?"
Mori took a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his coat. "I need to deliver this letter to Seifu by May eighteenth."
Haruka sighed to herself. It was the season for purchasing herbs, and she was so busy even a cat's help would have been welcome—and yet.
Even so, Haruka refused the money, saying only, "I'll guide you up the mountain early tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as dawn broke, the two set out. Haruka carried a basket on her back, containing rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

On the mountainside, they met an old man named Shigeru Tanaka, who had been splitting firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. Three strangers had been asking around at the entrance to town yesterday evening, he said, about a young man who had been injured.
"Haruka, take the back road," Tanaka said. "The main road is dangerous." Haruka thanked him.
The back road was narrow and slippery. Haruka took the lead, stepping carefully and deliberately, one step at a time. Mori followed in silence.

By midday the rain had stopped, and the mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the roof of Seifū-ji in the distance. A nun stood before the gate—a woman named Shizuka Yamamoto who handled visitors to the temple.
Yamamoto took the letter and, confirming the red seal on the envelope, nodded. "The head priest has been waiting two years for this letter."
Mori told Haruka, "You're our lifesaver." Haruka smiled and replied, "Well then, next time you come, fix the apothecary's roof for us." Mori stayed at the temple.
That evening, Haruka descended the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark. She lit a lamp and sat for a long while in the back of the shop.
